about: Shared trips: when a trip counts as being with the manager, and whose money each expense is. Both apps read this file in their tests. A trip is often made by one rep with colleagues tagged on, so 'whose is it' has to be answered the same way on a phone and on the web or two sheets disagree about what somebody spent.

fields.note: tagged_csv is pipe-wrapped Sales Person NAMES, e.g. |Pareeth Kb|. Sales Person.custom_team_manager is a short TOKEN, e.g. Pareeth. Comparing the two matches nothing - which is exactly the bug that made 'Shop visit with manager' read zero on every row until 18 Aug 2026.

with_manager.why: the rep made the trip and tagged the manager along - the live case, TRP-00258: Jaimon D's trip carrying |Pareeth Kb|
the manager made the trip and tagged the rep - the same journey, recorded from the other side, and it must count identically
the TOKEN must never be what is compared. 'Pareeth' is the team name; 'Pareeth Kb' is the record a trip tags, and passing the token silently counts nothing
somebody who was not on the trip did not travel with the manager, however many colleagues were
two reps travelling together without their manager is not a trip with the manager
a solo trip is not one either
a team with no identifiable manager counts nothing rather than everything

expenses.why: an expense tagged to somebody is theirs alone - the lunch one rep bought on a trip another rep is claiming
an untagged expense is COMMON to everyone who travelled - a toll or a tank of fuel belongs to the journey, not to whoever happened to key it in
an empty string is not a person - Frappe returns an unset Link three ways and none of them is an owner
the string 'null' from naive interpolation is not a person either

totals.why: each person is charged what was tagged to them, and the common pot is reported separately rather than divided - nobody asked for it to be split, and inventing a split would put money on a sheet that was never agreed

an expense tagged to somebody who is not on the trip is still counted in the trip total, and still shown against them - the tag is a statement about whose money it was, and dropping it would lose the amount entirely
a trip with nothing on it totals zero rather than failing
